mcq_choices.rationale: smaller moment of inertia requires larger angular speed
Incorrectly assumes energy, not angular momentum, is what's conserved; rotational KE actually increases as the arms pull in and do work against the centripetal force.
Misattributes the speed-up to a change in the skater's mass, when her mass is constant and only the mass distribution (and thus moment of inertia) changes.
Invents an irrelevant change in gravity rather than recognizing that pulling in the arms reduces the moment of inertia.

parts.prompt:
A skater pulls in her arms with negligible external torque. Her angular speed increases because

A. angular momentum is conserved
B. rotational kinetic energy is conserved
C. mass increases
D. gravity vanishes

criteria.description: Select the single scientifically correct answer.
required_evidence: smaller moment of inertia requires larger angular speed

review_notes.expected_reasoning: smaller moment of inertia requires larger angular speed
